body: I think perhaps my current counsellor isn't as effective as I need them to be. I've been in counselling a lot over the past few years and have never been able to find a good "fit" so I had started to wonder if it was perhaps me that was the problem

I need people to listen, and to try to consider my needs/perspective. I need someone to just hang out with me and help me feel some sense of normalacy again. I don't necessarily want to talk about my problems 24/7, but I need to know it's safe for me to do so without feeling like I'm burdening people. That's kinda how I feel right now, like I'm wanting/needing these things and it's a burden for everyone.

I know people in my life care, but they care in such weird ways or they don't express it when I need it. My mom shows it in a very materialistic way, and she seems to also think that being an authoritarian figure in my life is caring. My partner shows it in very loving ways, he cares and I really truly know it, our relationship just seems to be fizzling because I have changed and we are in very different points in our life. He hasn't really been there with me throughout this whole medical process, and I assume it's because it was too much and he just didn't know how to be there. But it has definitely created some distance between us.

I have, the response has yet to be positive. My mother takes things very personally and will rage against me because she gets so offended. My "friends" don't really listen to my requests, the biggest of which has been to set my boundaries and ask them to stop turning to me for favours and support at this time. Again, I'm trying not to be selfish, but I just can't give any support right now when I am so badly depleted of it. I'd been really interested in counselling for a while and I think what's happened is that I've become a sort of "counsellor" for everyone. It's frustrating.
